This contraction is not merely a short-term blip, as evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -16% [E14] alongside a scanX signal engine screen flagging a complete wipeout with sales down 100% year-on-year [E57]. Compounding these existential growth risks, the business offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], providing no income cushion for shareholders while navigating decelerating earnings growth [E58]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a low price-to-book ratio of 0.18x [E2] and recent profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 106% [E46], yet these metrics cannot mask a core business experiencing terminal, long-term revenue evaporation.

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is indeed -84% [E17] and 3-year sales growth is -54% [E16], alongside a 10-year sales decline of -16% [E14] and a year-on-year sales screen drop [E57]. However, the bear's focus on top-line contraction ignores a powerful counter-trend in profitability: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months surges by 74% [E21], and 5-year profit growth stands at a robust 56% [E19]. This fundamental earnings strength is driving actual outperformance, as profit growth recently exceeds 1-year price growth by 106% [E46]. Furthermore, while the bear highlights a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], the stock trades at an extraordinarily deep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.18x (price ₹ 0.19 on a book value of ₹ 1.07) [E2] and an alternative provider P/B of 0.11x against a sector benchmark of 1.2x [E7]. Finally, the 10-year compounded profit growth of 15% [E18] proves the business can generate lasting bottom-line expansion despite volatile revenues.

Conceded: the company posted 5-year compounded profit growth of 56% [E19] and 10-year compounded profit growth of 15% [E18]. However, the bull's reliance on bottom-line strength ignores a catastrophic, accelerating top-line collapse demonstrated by a trailing twelve month sales decline of -84% [E17], a 3-year sales contraction of -54% [E16], and a year-on-year sales plunge of -100% [E57]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at a low 0.18x [E2] or 0.11x [E7], but this asset backing is undermined by a high P/E ratio of 44.3 [E1] and explicit warnings that earnings growth is decelerating [E58]. Furthermore, the cited 74% TTM profit growth [E21] cannot be viewed in isolation when the broader 3-year profit trend has dropped by -33% [E20] and 5-year sales growth is flagged as poor at 9.16% [E51]. The absolute lack of dividend returns with a 0.00% yield [E4] leaves shareholders holding a contracting, low-growth asset where shrinking revenues and deceleration [E58] overwhelm any theoretical book value discount [E2].
